before: At 01:05 in Film Heritage Foundation’s restoration-comparison excerpt, an older man in white leans forward, his hands near his chin. The long back of his chair rises behind him, unoccupied by his body. Dark openings interrupt the pale wall around the seated figure.[^comparison-frame] The contrast is worth staying with: the chair offers room to lean back, while his posture carries him forward. Without deciding what he feels or naming the moment in the family’s story, we can notice how much of this image belongs to the house around him.
after: An older man sits towards the front of a long-backed chair, leaning forward, his hands near his chin. In this brief image from the restoration excerpt, dark openings punctuate a pale wall. The chair has room for him to recline; he does not use it. His posture draws our attention, but so does the space around him. How would the moment change if we saw only his face? The house would disappear.[^comparison-frame]
